messages:
tom: Hey all, first day hiccup. I unboxed my MacBook Pro (M2) and ran the Kandji enrollment, then updated to macOS 14.3. After reboot the machine drops me to a FileVault login loop and the company MDM profile never shows up in System Settings. Also seeing repeated prompts to allow "ThreatShield" EDR extension. Any idea who owns the fix?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @tom! :tada: IT handles device enrollment issues and security handles EDR whitelisting. Pinging them now.
it-support: Hey Tom 44b can you paste the output of these three commands so we can triage quickly:
`/usr/bin/fdesetup status`
`profiles status -type enrollment`
`system_profiler SPConfigurationProfileDataType | grep -i Kandji -A2`
Also did you migrate from an existing backup or use Migration Assistant?
tom: Output below:
`$ fdesetup status
FileVault is On.`
`$ profiles status -type enrollment
No mobile device management enrollment found.`
`$ sw_vers -productVersion
14.3`
I restored some documents from iCloud, did not do a full Migration Assistant restore.
sierra: Huh, FileVault is on but MDM didn't install. EDR often injects kernel/system extensions that can interfere with profile installs on upgrade. Quick plan: (A) we can grant a short temp-admin so IT can remove the EDR listener, push a targeted Kandji re-enroll, and then reprovision the FileVault escrow; or (B) security can whitelist the Kandji installer in the EDR console and we can push policy without touching the client. Which do you prefer?
security: From a security standpoint we prefer not to remove EDR agents. If Kandji can be allowed through the EDR console it prevents churn. However, given you're blocked on login loop today, we can do a supervised temporary disable of the EDR on that host while we reprovision via Kandji, with strict monitoring. We'll need the device serial and consent.
it-support: Temp-admin approach is faster for a single-device unblock. I can grant a 45-minute admin token and remote in. We'll run `sudo launchctl unload /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.threatshield.agent.plist` then push Kandji profile and run `sudo fdesetup changerecovery -personal` to escrow a new recovery key to Kandji backend. We'll coordinate with Security to re-enable the EDR afterward.
people-ops: Quick welcome from People Ops! :wave: If you need immediate VPN or SSO access restored for onboarding tasks, say the word and we can prioritize.
tom: I'm ok with the temp-admin plan if Security watches the change. I just want to be able to finish the initial checklist (VPN, git).
security: Agreed, we'll monitor and only allow the unload command on this serial while keeping telemetry streaming. Please DM your serial and confirm consent.
it-support: Granting temp-admin (45m) and scheduling a remote session now. Tom, when ready please keep the laptop plugged in and on the company network.
tom: Remote session started. Seeing the EDR unload and Kandji re-enroll prompt.
it-support: Re-enroll pushed, Kandji prompts accepted. Now running `profiles status -type enrollment` -> shows "Enrolled via Kandji (MDM) - profile active". Next step: reprovision FileVault escrow.
tom: After reprovisioning I got a new recovery key prompt and a Kandji notification that recovery key was escrowed. Rebooted and no more login loop.
security: Confirmed EDR agent reloaded and was re-applied with the Kandji whitelist rule in place for the installer. We logged the temporary unload and tied it to the admin session. No anomalous telemetry.
it-support: Closing the loop: enrollment succeeded, FileVault key escrowed, EDR present and whitelisted for Kandji on that host. If anything else blocks SSO/VPN or certs, ping #help or DM IT.
tom: All good now 60a Thanks everyone for the quick help and the warm welcome!
people-ops: Welcome aboard again @tom! :tada:
